data.title: Astro + Solid migration and English project language

events.goal: Take issue #9 through the whole process on your own
requirements: Read the task in full from the issue: the description and the comments
Do not wait for my approval of the plan; if the analyst has questions, pick the simpler and cleaner option, write the decision into the plan and go on
On the third return do not stop: decide yourself, simplify what does not work without bypassing the checks, and note it in the final report
Do not bypass or disable the checks
Commit in small commits and push
Write Closes #9 in the body of the commit that closes the task
When the task is done, run /publish-recording; I approve the draft and the tables in advance, so check them yourself by the skill rules and publish
Commit the recording, push, open a PR into main and merge it once CI is green
In the final report, tell me what changed with links to the screenshots, which decisions you made without me and what I have to do by hand

events.line: Take issue 9 and write the spec; no open questions
events.text:
Write the spec for issue 9 of the split-bill repository. The issue has no comments. It is the first of three tasks (new stack, then languages and SEO, then UX): move the interface to Astro with Solid and make English the project language. The look and behavior of the app must not change.

Stack: rewrite the interface as Solid components inside Astro. The page is static (SSG), the interactive parts are Solid islands, deployment stays on GitHub Pages with the /split-bill/ base path. Do not change the domain logic in the bill, settlement and sharing folders, and keep the ESLint ban on the DOM there. New dependencies are only astro, solid-js, @astrojs/solid-js and checking and testing tools, with no UI kits or CSS frameworks. Keep the interface style from AGENTS.md whole: tokens, themes, components, AA contrast, 44 px touch targets, reduced motion. Share links made by the old version (the bill in the fragment after #) must open in the new one, pinned by a test. Tests stay green, DOM tests move to Solid, astro check is added to make check, and CI and deployment are updated.

Project language: everything except interface text becomes English: code comments, commit messages (Conventional Commits fully in English), README, AGENTS.md, PR descriptions and new journal entries. Interface texts stay Russian for now. Update the language rules in AGENTS.md; old commits and past journal entries stay as they are.

Look check: Playwright screenshots at 360x800, 768x1024 and 1280x800, in light and dark theme, empty and filled, compared with the screenshots from before the migration. Fix differences and refresh the two screenshots in docs. Done when make check and CI are green, the site builds for GitHub Pages, the look and behavior are unchanged, old links open, and AGENTS.md and README describe the new stack and language.

The human approved the spec in advance and is unavailable. If questions come up, do not leave them open: choose the simpler and cleaner option, write the decision into a Decisions section and go on.

Notes for the plan: the network to npm works; use the preinstalled Chromium, do not run a Playwright install and do not add Playwright to the project; the screenshot script lives in a temporary directory outside the repository. Take the before screenshots from the current HEAD, for example in a separate worktree, and make that the first step. Generated harness files must not be edited by hand; check whether sync is needed after editing AGENTS.md. Split the work into small commits with green checks at each one, in English, the last one with Closes #9 in the body. Decide whether translating comments in the domain code counts as changing the domain logic.

Return the spec: goal, changes by file, plan of steps and commits, verifiable done criteria, decisions and risks.

events.line: Spec ready: six commits, 16 decisions, done criteria
events.text:
Spec for issue 9: move the interface to a static Astro page with one Solid island and translate everything except interface text into English. For the user the look and behavior stay the same, and old share links still open. A preliminary check of the stack in a scratch directory outside the repository passed: the build with the /split-bill/ base puts assets under the base path, astro check covers ts and tsx files, Solid tests in jsdom work with a dedicated Vitest config, and hydration in Chromium shows no console errors.

Decisions. There is exactly one island, the App component, because everything depends on one bill state and state libraries are forbidden. The server renders an empty bill; the address, hashchange, navigator and crypto are touched only after mount, so hydration does not diverge. The base path is /split-bill/ without a site address, which only the SEO task needs. The typecheck script becomes astro check. New dependencies are astro, solid-js and @astrojs/solid-js, plus @astrojs/check, @solidjs/testing-library, prettier-plugin-astro and eslint-plugin-solid for development; the direct vite dependency goes away. Configs are plain js files, component files are kebab-case tsx. The DOM does not change: same tags, classes, ids, attributes and order, hidden things stay hidden by the hidden attribute. The bill signal re-renders on every write, so section messages and the link field reset as before. The old accidental behavior stays: the summary content is recreated on each bill change and the How it was calculated block collapses. Form fields are controlled, and tests change only their input helpers, not their assertions. Comments, test names, internal error messages, ESLint messages, workflow names and the session hook are translated; this is not a change of domain logic. Generated harness files are not edited by hand; sync runs once after the dependencies are added to update the stack in the project config. The ESLint ban in the domain folders is extended to solid-js and astro imports. Workflows get English names, and there is no branch protection that could break. New journal entries are English only.

Plan. Step 0 takes the before screenshots from the current HEAD in a separate worktree: three widths, two themes, four states (empty, example, example with the breakdown open, stress), 24 in all, checking horizontal scroll, touch targets of at least 44 px and console errors. Commit 1 translates AGENTS.md and README, with the new language rule. Commit 2 translates comments, test names and internal messages. Commit 3 adds a test that opens a share link from the previous version by a literal code, still on the old interface. Commit 4 builds the site with Astro (config, page shell, tsconfig, prettier plugin, ignores, deployment comment, sync). Commit 5 rewrites the interface as a Solid island, with new components, a Vitest config, ESLint rules and migrated tests. Step 6 takes the after screenshots and compares them pixel by pixel, expecting zero differences, and also checks the index.html address and a query string. Commit 6 describes the new stack in AGENTS.md and README, refreshes the screenshots and closes the issue.

Done criteria. make check is green at each of the six commits; the built page has server markup with the heading, assets under the base path, the favicon, the theme color and the Russian language; only the listed dependencies are added and there is one vite version; the old-link test passes before and after the migration while other tests keep their cases and assertions; importing the DOM or solid-js in the domain folders fails lint; all 24 screenshot pairs match; code is in English except interface text, test data and the page title; generated files are untouched and sync check is clean; commits are Conventional Commits in English, the last with Closes #9; AGENTS.md and README describe the new stack.

Out of scope: interface translations and i18n, the site address and SEO, UX improvements, any change to the domain logic or link format, and translating generated harness files, old commits or past journal entries.

Risks. Two copies of solid-js in Vitest, which the dedicated config avoids. Hydration breaks if the address is read before mount. A select in Solid can lose its value if bound before the options appear, so the selected attribute is used. The For component reuses nodes, so the recipients signal must be reset. Whitespace nodes can shift inline layout, and the screenshots will show it. Astro needs Node 22.12 or newer. The _astro directory is safe on GitHub Pages because Actions deployment does not run Jekyll.

events.line: Got it. Before shots first, then the English docs
events.text:
The working copy is clean and the approved spec for issue 9 is in the scratchpad; read it in full. The work goes in parts, and your part now is only this.

Step 0, the before screenshots, with no changes in the repository. Keep the worktree and all files in the scratchpad: the worktree for the current version, a screenshot script and the images. Make the script parameterized by base address and output directory so the after screenshots can be taken with the same script. It must also save a JSON file with the check results: scroll width, touch targets smaller than 44 px, console errors. Stop the preview server when done, but do not remove the worktree yet.

Commit 1, translate AGENTS.md and README to English per the plan, with the new language rule. Keep the meaning, structure, contrast table and all rules in full. The stack description stays as it is for now. Then run the formatter and make check, which must be green.

Do not commit; the lead does that. Do not touch the generated harness files. In the report: what was done, where the script and screenshots are, the results of the before checks (whether the old version already has violations), the make check summary and any deviations from the plan.

events.line: Here: before shots done, docs translated, checks green
events.text:
The before screenshots (step 0) and commit 1, the translation of AGENTS.md and README, are ready. Nothing is committed, and make check is green.

Step 0. The worktree of the current version is in the scratchpad, with dependencies installed and the build done; it is not removed. The preview server was stopped and the port no longer answers. The screenshot script takes a base address and an output directory, and the same script will be used for the after shots. It uses the globally installed Playwright, with no browser install. The matrix of 3 widths, 2 themes and 4 states gives 24 full-page screenshots. A JSON file records, for each, the scroll width, horizontal scroll, touch targets under 44 px, the presence of the breakdown block, and console errors including warnings, page errors and failed requests. Result: on the old version there are no violations, no horizontal scroll, no small touch targets and no console errors. I looked at one screenshot by eye, the example at 360 px in the light theme with the breakdown open, and the layout is fine.

Commit 1. AGENTS.md is translated in full, with structure, all rules and the contrast table kept. Decimal commas became points and the table headers became Pair, Light and Dark. The language rule is written as in the plan: the interface is Russian for now, everything else is English, old commits and journal entries stay as they are, and the commit example is in English. The link to Conventional Commits now points to the English version. Russian interface strings stay as quoted literals with a translation in brackets. The stack description is unchanged. README is translated too, including image alt texts, and the title is now the Russian title of the app (Split the bill). Workflow names stay Russian with a translation in brackets until they are renamed in commit 2. The formatter changed only these two files and make check is green: 313 of 313 tests, build passed.

Deviations from the plan: I added one sentence to README, The interface is in Russian, because the interface is still Russian while the text is now English. It can be removed if not wanted. There are no other deviations.

events.line: Got it. Checking the translation against the original
events.text:
Review only commit 1, the translation of AGENTS.md and README to English, which is the uncommitted diff. The task is split into parts and this is the first one.

Check that the translation is complete and accurate: no rule, token, contrast table row, command or step is lost or distorted. Check that the new language rule matches the plan: the interface is Russian for now; everything else is English, including Conventional Commits fully in English, README, AGENTS.md, PR descriptions and new journal entries; old commits and past journal entries are not touched. The stack description is still the old one, which is expected; it will be updated in commit 6.

The coder's deviations to judge: README has a new sentence, The interface is in Russian; workflow names in README are still Russian with a translation in brackets and will be renamed in commit 2; decimal commas in the contrast table became points.

Verdict: DONE, or NEEDS REWORK with a list of remarks.

events.line: Accepted: translation is complete, two nitpicks only
events.text:
ACCEPTED (DONE)

I checked the uncommitted diff of AGENTS.md and README paragraph by paragraph against HEAD. There are no other changes or new files.

AGENTS.md is complete. All sections are in place with their meaning intact, including the About, Commands, Tasks, Code and tests, and Interface style parts with Tokens, Components, Rules and How to check the look. All color, avatar, radius, spacing and size tokens, the 900 px and 480 px thresholds, the WCAG requirements and the contrast formula are kept. All 17 rows of the contrast table are there with matching values. All component and style rules are kept, as are the five steps of the look check with their commands. Russian interface labels stay as they are with a translation in brackets, which is correct because they stay Russian in code.

The new language rule matches the plan: the interface is Russian for now, everything else is English, old commits and journal entries are untouched, and the link to the specification now points to the English version. The stack is still the old one, as expected. README is complete too, including image alt texts, and its link to the interface style section matches the AGENTS.md heading.

The coder's deviations are justified: the sentence about the Russian interface helps an English reader, the Russian workflow names match the current ones in the workflow files, and points in numbers are normal for English. make check is green, and Prettier is clean on both files. There are no secrets, server addresses or personal data.

Two minor remarks that do not block. In the last row of the contrast table one cell is not padded to the column width, which affects only the source view. Two bullets in a row start with the word Language; the first could say Programming language.

events.line: Understood. Translating comments, test names, messages
events.text:
Commit 1 was accepted by review and committed. The next part is commit 2, translating code comments, test names and internal messages to English, strictly by the plan. It covers the source folder, the stylesheet, the ESLint config, the names and comments of the workflows, and the session hook. Do not translate the old build config, the old page and the old entry file, except for the error message in the entry file.

After renaming the workflows, fix their names in README. Also a small thing from the review: in AGENTS.md change the first bullet from Language: TypeScript to Programming language: TypeScript. Then run the formatter and make check, which must be green. Do not commit and do not start anything from commit 3.

Report: the list of files, the make check result and deviations.

events.line: Here: commit 2 is ready, 41 files, checks green
events.text:
Commit 2 is ready and nothing is committed. The formatter and make check are green: format check, typecheck and lint are clean, tests pass 313 of 313 with the same set of cases, and the build passed.

What was translated to English, in 41 files with only modifications. Domain logic: comments and thrown error messages in the bill, settlement and sharing modules, including all 20 failure reasons in the bill code module. Interface: comments only, with interface texts untouched; in the entry file only the thrown error was translated. Tests: all describe and it names, case labels in each-tables, comments and error messages in helpers. Test data names and expected interface texts are untouched. Messages checked by tests were translated together with the tests, and a clipboard mock error became Access denied. Other files: all stylesheet comments, the ESLint comment and two ban messages, workflow names, job names and a comment in both workflows, and the comments and echo lines of the session hook. README now uses the new workflow names, and AGENTS.md has Programming language: TypeScript.

I did not touch the old build config, the old page, or the generated harness files. Nothing from commit 3 was done.

Deviations. Cyrillic remains only where it is interface text, test data or button names, as quoted literals inside English comments and test names, plus a middle dot and the ruble sign in the stylesheet. Test names that used guillemets now use plain quotes; Prettier replaced them itself.

events.line: Got it. Checking that it is translation only
events.text:
Review only commit 2, translating code comments, test names and internal messages to English, which is the uncommitted diff of 41 files. The task is done in parts.

Check that the changes are only translation: comments, describe and it names, internal error messages and reasons, ESLint messages, workflow and job names, the session hook and CSS comments. events.line: Sending back: three test names left in Russian
events.text:
NEEDS REWORK

What I checked. I compared the syntax tree of every changed script with HEAD, with comments removed and string literals replaced by a placeholder. The code matches in all 35 files and the number of string literals in each file is unchanged, so no logic was touched and only comments and string texts changed. I read all changed lines. Interface texts, test data names and expected interface texts stayed Russian. The clipboard mock error became Access denied, which is acceptable because it never reaches the interface. The old build config, the old page and the generated harness files are untouched. README has the new workflow names. The translation is accurate overall and make check is green: lint, 313 tests, build.

Remarks. First, three test names are not translated, probably because the name stands on a separate line after an each-table. These are the title of the describe for the Base64 URL encoding and decoding, the name and case labels of the maximum name length test in the bill code tests (the data values must stay), and the name and case labels of the test about links with repeated names and another version in the interface tests (the garbage fragment data must stay). Second, the AGENTS.md change from Language to Programming language does not belong to this commit; it is harmless but should be named as a deviation. Third, in the stylesheet the second line of two multi-line comments shifted and is misaligned. Fourth, one English comment in the bill module still has guillemets around an emoji sequence, while all others were replaced by plain quotes.

The remaining Cyrillic in comments is quotes of interface texts, and apart from them it remains only in the old build config, as the plan says.

events.line: Understood, fixing the three remarks from review

events.line: Understood. Moving the build to Astro, old UI inside
events.text:
Commit 3 is committed. The next part is commit 4, building the site with Astro for GitHub Pages, strictly by the plan: the old interface inside Astro, without Solid. Update package.json (add astro; add the check tool and the Prettier plugin for development; remove vite; Node 22.12 or newer; dev, build, preview and typecheck scripts on astro). Then run sync and leave the project config change in the working copy; list any other files sync changes.

Comments are in English. Check that the interface tests, which import the interface directly, work under Vitest without the Vite config; that there is one vite version; that the built page has assets under the base path, the favicon, the theme color and the Russian language; and that the preview opens the base path and an example code in Chromium without console errors. Run the formatter, make check must be green, do not commit. Report: files, versions, check results and deviations.

events.line: Commit 3 pushed; the worker is moving the build to Astro

events.goal: Tell me whether this task is done

events.line: Here: commit 4 ready, build on Astro, screenshots match
events.text:
Commit 4 is ready and nothing is committed. The formatter and make check are green: format check, astro check with no errors, warnings or hints, lint, 314 of 314 tests, and the Astro build.

Versions. astro 7.3.7 is in dependencies; @astrojs/check 0.9.10 and prettier-plugin-astro 1.1.0 are in development dependencies; the direct vite dependency is removed. There is one vite version, 8.3.3, which comes through astro, vitefu and vitest.

Files. package.json now requires Node 22.12 or newer and its dev, build, preview and typecheck scripts use astro; the lock file is updated. A new Astro config sets the /split-bill/ base with an English comment explaining why. A new page repeats the old shell: Russian language, charset, viewport, theme color, the Russian title of the app, the main element, the favicon through the base URL, and the old interface connected by a script. The old index page and Vite config are removed with git. tsconfig extends the strict Astro preset and keeps the four old flags. The Prettier config uses the Astro plugin, and the Astro cache directory is added to the three ignore places. The comment in the deployment workflow now says the checks already include the Astro build into dist, and the published path is unchanged. After sync the stack in the project config became astro, which stays in the working copy; sync changed nothing else and its check returns 0.

Checks. The interface tests and the rest work under Vitest without any Vite config. The built page has the Russian language, the theme color, the favicon under the base path, and CSS and JS under the base path assets; the main element is still empty because the old interface is drawn by a script. In the preview, the base path and the favicon answer 200. With the same script I took all 24 screenshots, including the example and stress codes: no console errors, no horizontal scroll, no touch targets under 44 px. The 24 screenshots are byte-identical to the before ones. The preview server is stopped.

Deviations: none. One side note: another process, a preview from an unrelated scratch directory, is running on a different port; I did not touch it.

events.line: Got it. Reviewing commit 4 against the plan

events.line: Sending back: lock file still says Node 22
events.text:
NEEDS REWORK

One small thing must be fixed; everything else in commit 4 is fine.

Remark 1. In the root entry of the lock file, the Node engine is still at least 22, while package.json already says at least 22.12. The lock file does not match package.json. A clean install does not fail on this, but the first plain install by anyone will rewrite the lock file and leave a stray change in the working copy. Fix it by updating only the lock file and checking that just this line changed.

Two trifles you may leave. The page has an empty frontmatter, which Astro does not need, but imports will land there in commit 5 anyway. And the Astro cache directory is written in the ignore file without a trailing slash, unlike its neighbors.

For information, not part of this commit: AGENTS.md still describes Vite and Node 22, and the preview command from the look-check section does not work at this step because assets now have the absolute /split-bill/ path. Until commit 6, view the page through the Astro preview at the base path.

What matched. The plan for commit 4 is followed: the scripts call astro and typecheck is astro check; the Node engine is 22.12 or newer; the config has the base path without a site address and an English comment explaining it; the page repeats the old one; the old index page and the Vite config are removed; the Prettier plugin and the ignores are in place; only the deployment comment changed and dist is still published. Dependencies are exactly those of decision 5 and there is one vite version. tsconfig has the strict preset and the four old flags, and astro check reports no errors in 37 files. make check passes. The built page has the Russian language, the theme color, the favicon and assets under the base path. The project config changed only in the stack field, and the sync check returns 0. The generated harness files are untouched, and there are no secrets or personal data. I did not re-run the screenshots myself.

events.line: Understood. Rewriting the UI as a Solid island
events.text:
The working copy is clean and the approved spec for issue 9 is in the scratchpad; read it in full, especially the decisions and risks. Commits 1 to 4 are done: English docs and comments, the old-link test, and the Astro build with the old interface connected by a script.

Your part is commit 5, rewriting the interface as a Solid island, and step 6, the after screenshots, strictly by the plan. Add solid-js and @astrojs/solid-js, and for development @solidjs/testing-library and eslint-plugin-solid; enable the Solid integration; set the JSX options in tsconfig; add the verified Vitest config from the plan; in ESLint add the Solid rules for tsx files and ban solid-js and astro imports in the domain folders. Write the components in the interface folder as planned, with one island, App, and delete the old entry file, the DOM helpers, the section helper and all create functions. Do not change the address, plural and settlement explanation modules or the domain folders. The DOM must stay the same (decision 8) and so must the behavior (decisions 9 to 11). Tests: the interface test and avatar test become tsx files; only mounting and input helpers change, with fireEvent, and the set of cases and assertions stays, including the old-link test. Run sync so the project config gets solid. Comments are in English, interface texts stay Russian, and follow the CLAUDE.md rules on names, one action per function, no nested calls in arguments and named conditions.

Screenshots: use the existing script and the before screenshots. After the build, start the Astro preview in the background, take the after screenshots in the scratchpad with the base path, compare them pixel by pixel with pixelmatch and pngjs installed in a separate scratchpad directory, not in the project, and fix any differences. The goal is zero different pixels in all 24 pairs, no console or hydration errors, no horizontal scroll and touch targets of at least 44 px. Also check that the index.html address and an address with a query string open. Stop the preview afterward. Note that the Vite preview does not fit because of the base path. The built page must contain server markup with the heading in the main element.

Finish with the formatter and a green make check. Do not commit. Do not touch the generated harness files, AGENTS.md or README. Report: files, make check, the differing pixel count for each pair, dist checks, and deviations with reasons.

events.line: Here: Solid island done, 24 screenshots identical
events.text:
Commit 5 and step 6 are done. make check is green after the formatter: format check, astro check with no errors or warnings, lint, 11 files with 314 tests, and the Astro build. Nothing is committed and the preview is stopped.

Configuration. solid-js and @astrojs/solid-js are added to dependencies and @solidjs/testing-library and eslint-plugin-solid to development, in the planned versions, with one vite version still. The Astro config enables the Solid integration, tsconfig has the JSX options, and a new Vitest config has the planned conditions and inline dependencies with a comment explaining why. ESLint has the Solid rules for tsx files and bans solid-js and astro imports in the domain logic; I checked by hand that a domain file importing solid-js and using document gives two lint errors.
